text.p: The Turkish central bank issued heavy funding on Friday through money and overnight repo deals to meet banks's cash shortage, following Wednesday's hefty auction payments, bankers said.
The bank lent 40.5 trillion lira overnight at 72 percent, 10.4 trillion lira via tomorrow/next deals at 71 percent and one trillion lira via tomorrow/week deals at 72 percent.
The central bank raised the tom/next and tom/week rates by one percentage point at the opening to block arbitrage possibilities between banks' overnight and tomorrow borrowings.

Bankers said the central bank's rate move pushed up bond prices after a weak opening caused by lower-than-expected June inflation data released early on Friday. The bank also injected a small amount of cash via overnight repos at 80 percent in the afternoon, they said.

"The central bank signalled that it will not allow the money market to relax in the coming days. Although bond yields fell at the opening on lower-than-expected inflation, the central bank's rate rise in the money market and the severe cash shortage quickly reversed this trend," said a banker.

Wholesale prices rose 3.4 percent month-on-month and consumer prices climed 2.9 percent in June, compared with 5.2 percent and 4.7 percent, respectively in May. Earlier June inflation forecasts in the market were within the 3.5 and 4.5 percent range.
In the bond market, the most heavily traded April 1, 1998 paper yielded 106.82 percent, up from 105.84 at Thursday's close. The yield had eased to 105.47 percent in early trade on the inflation data.
Bankers said uncertainty over a treasury bond auction expected next week as well as caution before a confidence vote in the new government also caused the bond yields to firm.
The right-left coalition of conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz, which was set up on Monday, will face a confidence vote in parliament on July 12.

The average overnight money rate on the screen-based, central-bank brokered interbank market increased to 71.95 percent from Thursday's 71.66. Overnight money rates were as high as 77 percent on the over-the-counter market, bankers said.
The average overnight repo rate also closed higher at 78.30 percent on Friday, versus a previous 77.62.

The lira weakened to 150,200 to the dollar from 149,400 at Thursday's close, in line with the dollar/mark parity and the central bank's key dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers for lira.
The bank raised its key dollar rate to 150,200 at close, from 150,100 at the opening and 149,400 on Thursday.
